translationRepairs: During the Xiande reign Deyi led a force that captured Hexia Town and took more than five hundred heads among the Bing army.
During the Xiande reign Deyi led a force that captured Heshi Town and took more than five hundred heads among the Bing army.
河市鎮 is Heshi Town; Hexia reads 市 as 下 and is a place-name error.
In Xiande, Deyi led troops to attack and take Hexia Town, beheading more than five hundred Bing troops.
In Xiande, Deyi led troops to attack and take Heshi Town, beheading more than five hundred Bing troops.
The same Hexia error appears in the literal field; 河市鎮 is Heshi Town.

During Taizong's Hedong campaign Yu Qing and Yin Xian were ordered to attack Lanzhou together; they routed the Kela garrison, captured its commander Zhe Lingtu, took the city, killed prefect Huo Yi, and seized seven officers including Ma Yanzhong.

During Taizong's Hedong campaign Yu Qing and Yin Xian were ordered to attack Lan Prefecture together; they routed the Kelan garrison, captured its commander Zhe Lingtu, took the city, killed Huo Yi, prefect of Xianzhou, and seized seven officers including Ma Yanzhong.
嵐州 is Hedong Lan Prefecture, not 蘭州 Lanzhou, and 岢嵐 is Kelan, but the proposed sentence still makes Huo Yi prefect of the captured city. 憲州刺史霍翊 is prefect of Xianzhou.

When Taizong campaigned in Hedong he ordered Yu Qing and Yin Xian to lead garrison troops jointly to attack Lanzhou; they again defeated the Kela Army, captured its military commissioner Zhe Lingtu and presented him, then took Lanzhou, also killed its prefect Huo Yi, and also captured seven of its generals including Ma Yanzhong.

When Taizong campaigned in Hedong he ordered Yu Qing and Yin Xian to lead garrison troops jointly to attack Lan Prefecture; they again defeated the Kelan Army, captured its military commissioner Zhe Lingtu and presented him, then took Lan Prefecture, also killed Huo Yi, prefect of Xianzhou, and also captured seven of its generals including Ma Yanzhong.
Lan Prefecture and Kelan Army are correct, but its prefect Huo Yi still attaches 霍翊 to 嵐州. The Chinese is 憲州刺史霍翊.

Soon afterward more than ten thousand Khitan raided; Yu Qing crushed them at Zihe Yi, taking five thousand heads and a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers bearing titles such as Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli were killed, and one Tuyuhun captive was taken—from then on the Khitan learned to fear him.

Soon afterward more than ten thousand Khitan raided; Yu Qing crushed them at Zihecha, taking five thousand heads and a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers bearing titles such as Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli were killed, and one Tuyuhun captive was taken—from then on the Khitan learned to fear him.
子河汊 is Zihecha; Yi is not a reading of 汊.

Soon after, more than ten thousand Khitan invaded; Yu Qing greatly defeated them at Zihe Yi, beheading five thousand, capturing a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers titled Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli died, and one Tuyuhun was captured—from then on the Khitan knew fear.

Soon after, more than ten thousand Khitan invaded; Yu Qing greatly defeated them at Zihecha, beheading five thousand, capturing a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers titled Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli died, and one Tuyuhun was captured—from then on the Khitan knew fear.
The literal field has the same 子河汊 transcription error.
A year later Yu Qing fell ill; Han Dewei learned of it through spies and, urged on by Li Jiqian, led a force to raid in revenge for Zihe Yi.
A year later Yu Qing fell ill; Han Dewei learned of it through spies and, urged on by Li Jiqian, led a force to raid in revenge for Zihecha.
報子河汊之役 refers to the same place; Zihe Yi is a mistranscription.
After more than a year Yu Qing fell ill; Dewei learned it by spies and, moreover incited by Li Jiqian, led a host to invade to avenge the battle of Zihe Yi.
After more than a year Yu Qing fell ill; Dewei learned it by spies and, moreover incited by Li Jiqian, led a host to invade to avenge the battle of Zihecha.
The literal revenge clause should read Zihecha for 子河汊.
In the ninth month Wan Sibao, a follower of Baoji, moved to Yimai and raided again. Weichang, Song Sigong, and Liu Wenzhi fought him at Maijing Peak and drove him off.
In the ninth month Wan Sibao Yimai, a follower of Baoji, came to raid again. Weichang, Song Sigong, and Liu Wenzhi fought him at Maijing Peak and drove him off.
萬私保移埋 is one personal name, not motion toward a place Yimai, but Wan Sibaoyimai is an unreadable run-on. Wan Sibao Yimai keeps all four characters.
In the ninth month, Wan Sibao of Baoji's faction moved to Yimai and again came to raid; Weichang with Song Sigong and Liu Wenzhi joined battle at Maijing Peak and routed them.
In the ninth month, Wan Sibao Yimai of Baoji's faction came to raid again; Weichang with Song Sigong and Liu Wenzhi joined battle at Maijing Peak and routed them.
Same name-split error in the literal field; use Wan Sibao Yimai rather than the fused Wan Sibaoyimai.
When Weiming Shan defected, Jishi learned of it first and sent his son Keqin to inform Chong Shi, who thereby captured Suizhou.
When Weiming Shan defected, Jishi learned of it first and sent his son Keqin to inform Chong E, who thereby captured Suizhou.
种諤 is Chong E; 諤 is È, not Shi.
When Chong Shi was imprisoned on criminal charges, Jishi was given his troops and, together with Weiming Shan, held Suizhou; for his service he was made prefect of Zhongzhou.
When Chong E was imprisoned on criminal charges, Jishi was given his troops and, together with Weiming Shan, held Suizhou; for his service he was made prefect of Zhongzhou.
The subject 諤 is the same Chong E named in the previous unit.

The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall and made the region Xi'anzhou; Keshi was promoted to eastern upper gate envoy, defense commissioner of Mingzhou, Jingyuan commander, and prefect, then confirmed as defense commissioner of Hezhou and observation commissioner of Mingzhou, and made deputy overall commander.

The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall and made the region Xi'anzhou; Keshi was promoted to eastern upper gate envoy, defense commissioner of Mingzhou (Hebei), Jingyuan commander, and prefect, then confirmed as defense commissioner of Hezhou and observation commissioner of Mingzhou (Zhejiang), and made deputy overall commander.
洺州 and 明州 are different prefectures that share the English Mingzhou. Tagging both as Mingzhou (Ming) does not distinguish them; Hebei names 洺州 and Zhejiang names 明州.
Chuan proposed taking Lingwu and Huanqing and requested reinforcements; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen and advanced to the banks of the Lingzhou River.
Chuan proposed taking Lingwu; Huanqing also requested to send troops; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen and advanced to the banks of the Lingzhou River.
環慶，亦請出師 makes Huanqing a second petitioner for a campaign, not a second place Chuan proposed to take. 慶兵不至 in the next sentence confirms Qing troops were expected as allies.

The transport commissioner asked to build separate stockyards at the four forts of Pingxia, Tongxia, Zhenrong, and Xi'an, setting five million bundles of fodder; Keshi objected that the expense was too great; he also wished to borrow carts and oxen to transport, and to deliver a hundred thousand hu to Xihe—all contrary to his intent; he was then struck with suspicion and slander, and was summoned as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.

The transport commissioner asked to build separate stockyards at the four forts of Pingxia, Tongxia, Zhenrong, and Xi'an, setting five million bundles of fodder; Keshi objected that the expense was too great; the commissioner also wished to borrow carts and oxen for transport and to deliver a hundred thousand hu to Xihe—all contrary to Keshi's intent; he was then struck with suspicion and slander, and was summoned as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.
After 可適以費大難之, 又欲借車牛以運 and 致十萬斛於熙河 continue the transport commissioner's proposals, which 皆戾其意 says ran against Keshi's intent.
The next year he was again appointed to Wei; his son Yanzhi was made a direct secretary in the Secretariat; he died several months later at sixty-one.
The next year he was again appointed to Wei; his son Yanzhi was made a collator of the Secret Cabinet attached to the military staff; he died several months later at sixty-one.
直秘閣參軍事 is a Secret Cabinet collatorship with a military-staff posting, not a Secretariat secretaryship.

Under Emperor Gong, Jiye had killed his brother to seize his father's command and grew arrogant, raiding Qiang and Yi tribes until they would not submit; he also showed little kindness to his troops and, fearing mutiny, moved their families to the capital because Taizu had once served under his father in the same circuit.

Under Emperor Gong, Jiye had killed his brother to seize his father's command and grew arrogant, raiding Qiang and Yi tribes until they would not submit; he also showed little kindness to his troops and, fearing mutiny, moved their families to the capital beforehand, because when Taizu had been stationed in the circuit Jiye had often been able to serve him.
太祖居鎮日常得給事 means that when Taizu held the circuit Jiye had often been able to serve him, not that Taizu had served under Jiye's father.

In the time of Emperor Gong, Jiye, having killed his brother and replaced his father in command of the circuit, was quite arrogant and willful, often sending troops to raid Qiang and Yi; the Qiang and Yi did not attach themselves; he also treated troops with little kindness; Jiye feared they would mutiny; because Taizu when stationed in the circuit had often been able to serve him, he beforehand moved their families to the capital.

In the time of Emperor Gong, Jiye, having killed his brother and replaced his father in command of the circuit, was quite arrogant and willful, often sending troops to raid Qiang and Yi; the Qiang and Yi did not attach themselves; he also treated troops with little kindness; Jiye feared they would mutiny; because when Taizu was stationed in the circuit Jiye had often been able to serve him, he beforehand moved their families to the capital.
The original literal makes Taizu the subject of 給事; the servant is Jiye.

Jiye in youth was clever and intelligent, with breadth of mind; through his father's appointment he was made envoy of the Shuofang military commission; he followed his father through Bin and Meng, and when he again held Shuofang, all were made staff posts.

Jiye in youth was clever and intelligent, with breadth of mind; through his father's appointment he was made envoy of the Shuofang military commission; he followed his father through Bin and Meng, and when his father again held Shuofang, Jiye was in each case given a staff post.
及再領朔方，皆補牙職 continues Jiye's career under his father: at each successive command, including Hui's return to Shuofang, Jiye received a staff post.
He appointed Fuxiang Kelangmai, second chief of the Qidang, Guide Langjiang; Yueyi, great chief of Meixi, Great General for Pacification; and Wayao Great Guide General.
Fuxiang Kelangmai, second chief of the Qidang, was made Guide Langjiang; Yueyi, great chief of Meixi, was made Great General for Pacification; and Wayao was made Great Guide General.
以…為 records three court titles. 瓦窯 is the personal name and 歸德大將軍 the office; the original fuses them and makes Chengmei the appointer.
In the sixth year his sons Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were enrolled in office.
In the sixth year his son Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were enrolled in office.
其子文寶 is one son; the plural sons is a number error.

Li Jifu, who had submitted at the same time as Jizhou, was made garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, rose through battle to Guide General and prefect of Shunzhou, and eventually became honored inner palace attendant and overall inspector of the newly submitted Ming tribes.

Li Jifu, who had submitted at the same time as Jizhou, was made garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, rose through battle to Guide General and prefect of Shunzhou, and eventually became honored inner palace attendant and overall inspector of the newly submitted tribes.
新歸明諸族 are newly submitted tribes; 歸明 is the submission term, not an ethnic name Ming.

Li Jifu also came over at the same time as Jizhou, was appointed garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, through battle merit rose to Guide General, held the prefecture of Shunzhou, and reached inner palace attendant of the honored class and overall inspector of the Newly Submitted Ming tribes.

Li Jifu also came over at the same time as Jizhou, was appointed garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, through battle merit rose to Guide General, held the prefecture of Shunzhou, and reached inner palace attendant of the honored class and overall inspector of the newly submitted tribes.
The literal field invents the same Ming ethnonym from 歸明.
In the mountain orchid temple was a nun, surname Sun, name Shenyi, who had arts that deluded the multitude.
In the mountain monastery was a nun, surname Sun, name Shenyi, who had arts that deluded the multitude.
蘭若 is a Buddhist monastic dwelling (āraṇya), not an orchid temple. Vihara transcribes a different word; monastery is the natural English equivalent here.
After the nun died in custody, Xingyou treated her cult with even greater awe, lighting incense by her rites until his following steadily grew.
After the nun died sitting in meditation, Xingyou treated her cult with even greater awe, lighting incense by her rites until his following steadily grew.
坐亡 is a seated Buddhist death, not death in legal custody.
When the nun died in custody, Xingyou made her affairs still more miraculous, and by her arts lit incense lamps; the gathering of people gradually grew.
When the nun died while seated, Xingyou made her affairs still more miraculous, and by her arts lit incense lamps; the gathering of people gradually grew.
The literal custody reading of 坐亡 is the same error.
In 962 he moved his stores, gathered fighting men, repaired arms, and prepared to return to Wolf Mountain to fortify himself.
In 961 he moved his stores, gathered fighting men, repaired arms, and prepared to return to Wolf Mountain to fortify himself.
建隆元年 is 960, so 建隆二年 is 961, not 962.
Fearing Quanzhao's stubborn nature would clash with Mu Xing, the court replaced him with Cao Shen.
Fearing Quanzhao's stubborn nature would clash with Mu Xing, the court replaced him with Cao Can.
曹璨 is Cao Can (璨 Càn). Cao Shen is 曹參, a different name.
Quanzhao owned a villa in Xuzhou, asked to govern that prefecture, and was granted his request.
Quanzhao owned a villa in Xu Prefecture, asked to govern that prefecture, and was granted his request.
許州 is Xu Prefecture; Xuzhou is 徐州.
Then, fearing that Quanzhao by nature was stubborn and obstinate and would not harmonize with Xing, Cao Shen was used to replace him.
Then, fearing that Quanzhao by nature was stubborn and obstinate and would not harmonize with Xing, Cao Can was used to replace him.
The literal field has the same 曹璨 name error.
Quanzhao had a villa in Xuzhou; he asked to govern that prefecture, and it was granted.
Quanzhao had a villa in Xu Prefecture; he asked to govern that prefecture, and it was granted.
The literal field likewise mistakes 許州 for 徐州.
